footerNote: EPS is shown exactly as reported in the release — GAAP diluted EPS of $4.42 — on a pre-split basis. The 10-for-1 forward stock split was announced in this same release, with split-adjusted trading expected to commence on July 15, 2024, so later filings restate this quarter's EPS as $0.44. All figures are GAAP, in $ millions unless noted; free cash flow is cash from operations of $4,580M less $132M of capital expenditures.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $2,343M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,516M inside cost of revenue and $827M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $5,394M instead of $2,121M.

Restructuring and other charges totaled $345M ($53M inside cost of revenue and $292M inside operating expenses), and the non-GAAP reconciliation also adds back $90M of acquisition-related costs and a $22M loss on debt extinguishment — the costs of integrating VMware.
The tax line was a $116M benefit, not an expense — it added to profit instead of subtracting from it. Broadcom's non-GAAP tax provision for the same quarter was $823M.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $1,047M on Broadcom's debt, much of it taken on to buy VMware, partly offset by $87M of other income — a net -$960M below operating profit.

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI products revenue was a record $3.1B in the quarter.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the jump is VMware, acquired in November 2023 and included for the full quarter, as more enterprises adopted the VMware stack to build their own private clouds.

takeaways.text: Revenue from AI products was a record $3.1B — roughly 43% of all semiconductor revenue — driven by custom accelerators and networking gear for data centers, and management raised full-year guidance on the strength of AI and VMware.
takeaways.title: AI demand set a record

takeaways.text: Infrastructure software revenue rose 175% to $5.3B — 42% of all revenue, up from 22% a year ago — because VMware was included for a full quarter, giving Broadcom a large subscription software business alongside its chips.
takeaways.title: VMware remade the mix

takeaways.text: GAAP net income fell 39% to $2.1B despite revenue rising 43%, weighed down by $2,343M of acquisition amortization, $345M of restructuring charges and $1,047M of interest expense. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $5,394M.
takeaways.title: Profit fell even as sales soared

verdict: Broadcom's revenue jumped 43% to $12.5B as VMware made software nearly half the company and AI chip sales hit a record, but the cost of absorbing VMware pulled GAAP profit down to $2.1B.
